newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: APEC leaders under pressure to produce results.
newsitem.headline: APEC leaders under pressure to produce results.

text.p: Pacific Rim leaders have headed home from the APEC summit under pressure to move forward their vision of a free trade Asia-Pacific area in the coming century embracing half the world's people.

"So far, there have been more words than deeds. But from 1997 onwards progress will have to mean more deeds than words," Edgardo Boeninger, Chilean chairman of the Pacific Economic Cooperation Council (PECC), said on Tuesday.

"The next few years will be crucial," he told a news conference summing up the six-day Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) conference that culiminated with a summit of leaders of its 18 members on Monday.

"If by the year 2000 substantial progress has not been made towards its goals... the credibility of APEC will suffer and the leadership of APEC can provide on the world scene will be very much limited," he added.
He said, however, he believed the Manila meetings at which APEC launched its action plan aimed at free trade and investment in the region by 2020 "has been a remarkable success".
The summit, at the former U.S. naval base at Subic Bay north of Manila, handed U.S. President Bill Clinton a victory on liberalising trade in information technology.

Clinton's fellow leaders gave him qualified support for his plan to scrap tariffs on trade in computers, memory chips and telcommunications equipment worth an annual $500 billion. But the president hailed it as "big deal" that would boost U.S. exports and create higher-paying jobs.
The Philippines official delegate to APEC, Edsel Custodio, said the Manila Action Plan for APEC (MAPA) adopted by the summit was "the first step in that long process of community building".

"It means a long process of closer consultation, close consensus and individual willingness to put on the table concrete measures on a voluntary basis, measures that will really help the other party....," he said.

Kim Kihwan, head of the Korea PECC committee and chairman of the board of directors of the (South) Korea Trade Promotion Corporation, said APEC as a purely voluntary organisation depended on "peer pressure" to maintain its momentum.

He foresaw beneficial effects of APEC on the first ministerial meeting in Singapore next month of the World Trade Organisation (WTO), which regulates world trade following the Uruguay Round of trade negotiations.
Kim said that the 18 APEC economies were in fact reducing their tariff rates faster than called for under the Uruguay Round.
This had great significance for the WTO in that other countries would be under pressure to match APEC, he said.
The fifth annual APEC summit will be in Vancouver, Canada, in November next year.

Former Philippine foreign secretary Roberto Romulo, chairman of the APEC Business Advisory Council, welcomed the statement by APEC leaders that they had "engaged the business sector in the APEC process".
"From our perspective, we found these words encouraging," said Romulo, who also chairs the countries giant long-distance telecommunications company.
"We must develop a strong proivate-poublic sector partnership to build a strong Asia-Pacific community," he said.
But he also said there was a pressing need to deepend the spirit of community so it touched all sectors of society through economic and tehnical cooperation.
"The human face of development, that sums it up as far as we are looking at it," he said.
